q.t: odd + odd = ?
q.e: Each odd number has one leftover; the two leftovers make a pair, so the sum is even.

q.t: even + odd = ?
q.e: The even number is all pairs; the odd number's single leftover stays unpaired.

q.t: What is the 100th odd number?
q.e: The 100th even number is 200; odd numbers sit one below the evens → 199. Formula 2n − 1.

q.t: What is the nth even number?
q.e: Even numbers are the 2-times table: 2, 4, 6, … → 2n.

q.t: In a 1–9 magic square, what is the magic sum?
q.e: All rows together use 1 + 2 + … + 9 = 45. Three equal rows → 45 ÷ 3 = 15.

q.t: Which number must be in the centre of a 1–9 magic square?
q.e: Any other centre makes some line impossible (e.g. 9 with 8 is already 17). Opposite pairs through the centre add to 10.

q.t: Next Virahāṅka number: 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, …
q.e: Each number is the sum of the two before it: 8 + 13 = 21.

q.t: A bulb is ON. Its switch is toggled 77 times. Is it on or off?
q.e: Every 2 toggles bring it back to ON. 77 is odd, so one toggle is left over → OFF.

q.t: Is the number of small squares in a 27 × 13 grid odd or even?
q.e: A product is odd only when all factors are odd. 27 and 13 are both odd.

q.t: In the height line, who always calls out 0?
q.e: Nobody stands in front of the first person, so nobody in front can be taller.

q.t: Can 5 odd numbers add up to 30?
o: No — an odd count of odd numbers gives an odd sum
Only if they are all equal
q.e: Two odds pair up their leftovers; with 5 odds one leftover remains, so the sum is odd. 30 is even.

q.t: Martin and Maria were born exactly a year apart. Can their ages add up to 112?
o: No — consecutive numbers add to an odd number
q.e: One of two consecutive numbers is even and one odd, so the sum is odd. 112 is even.

q.t: odd − even = ?
q.e: Taking away pairs doesn't touch the single leftover.

q.t: Is the sum of 8 odd numbers odd or even?
q.e: 8 is an even count, so all the leftovers pair up.

q.t: In a group of 8 people in a line, what is the largest number anyone can call out?
q.e: The shortest person standing last has all 7 others in front, all taller.

q.t: How many ways can 5 be written as an ordered sum of 1s and 2s?
q.e: Start with 1+ (then 4 beats: 5 ways) or 2+ (then 3 beats: 3 ways) → 5 + 3 = 8.

q.t: In T + T + T = UT, what digit is T?
q.e: 3 × T must end in T and be 2-digit: 3 × 5 = 15 → T = 5, U = 1.

q.t: Each number of a magic square is increased by 1. The magic sum 15 becomes…
q.e: Each line has 3 numbers, each up by 1, so every line sum goes up by 3.

q.t: The row sums of a 3 × 3 grid filled with 1–9 always add up to…
q.e: Adding all rows adds every number once: 1 + 2 + … + 9 = 45.

q.t: Which expression is always odd (n a counting number)?
q.e: 2n is even; even + 1 is odd. 3n + 4 depends on n; the others are always even.

q.t: In K2 + K2 = HMM, what is K?
q.e: Units 2 + 2 = 4 so M = 4. Then K + K must end in 4 with a carry: 2K = 14 → K = 7 (72 + 72 = 144).

q.t: Lakpa has an odd number of ₹1 coins, an odd number of ₹5 coins and an even number of ₹10 coins. Can his total be ₹205?
o: No — the total must be even
Only if he has no ₹10 coins
q.e: Odd × 1 = odd, odd × 5 = odd, even × 10 = even. Odd + odd + even = even, but 205 is odd.

q.t: How many rhythms of 8 beats (short = 1 beat, long = 2) are there?
q.e: 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21, 34 — the 8th Virahāṅka number.

q.t: Can 1 sit in a corner of a 1–9 magic square?
o: No — a corner is on 3 lines, but only 2 pairs add to 14 with 1
q.e: 1 would need three different pairs summing to 14 from 2–9; only 5 + 9 and 6 + 8 exist.

q.t: General magic square with centre m: what does every line add up to?
q.e: Each line is m plus pairs like +3 and −3 that cancel, leaving m + m + m = 3m.

q.t: What centre number makes a magic square with magic sum 60?
q.e: Magic sum = 3 × centre, so centre = 60 ÷ 3 = 20.

q.t: What comes after 55, 89 in the Virahāṅka sequence?
Is 6j − 4 (j = 1, 2, 3, …) a formula for ALL even numbers?
o: Yes, but only for big j
q.e: Steps of 6 skip most even numbers. All evens need steps of 2: 2n.

q.t: In YY + Z = ZOO, what is Y?
q.e: The sum is at most 99 + 9 = 108, so Z = 1 and ZOO = 100. YY = 99 → Y = 9.

q.t: Parity of 135 × 654?
q.e: 654 is even. If any factor is even, the product is even.

q.t: Is the 20th Virahāṅka number odd or even?
q.e: Parities go O, E, O, O, E, O, … — evens at positions 2, 5, 8, …, 20 (every 3rd from the 2nd).

q.t: Two consecutive Virahāṅka numbers are 987 and 1597. What is the number before 987?
q.e: 1597 = 987 + (previous), so previous = 1597 − 987 = 610.

q.t: Angaan climbs 8 steps taking 1 or 2 at a time. How many ways?
q.e: Same as rhythms of 8 beats. Each count is the sum of the previous two: … 13, 21, 34.

q.t: In UT + TA = TAT, what is U?
q.e: Two 2-digit numbers make less than 200, so T = 1. Units 1 + A ends in 1 → A = 0. U1 + 10 = 101 → U = 9.

q.t: In B5 + 3D = ED5, what is B?
q.e: Units: 5 + D ends in 5 → D = 0. B5 + 30 has 3 digits → E = 1 and B + 3 = 10 → B = 7 (75 + 30 = 105).

q.t: 50 loose book sheets, each with two consecutive page numbers. Is the total of page numbers odd or even?
q.e: Each sheet's two pages (one odd, one even) add to an odd number. 50 odd numbers — an even count — add to an even total.

q.t: A 3 × 3 grid of 1–9 has a row sum circled as 26. Possible?
o: No — the largest possible sum is 9 + 8 + 7 = 24
Only if 9 is in that row
q.e: Three different numbers from 1–9 add to at most 24 and at least 6.

q.t: Is the sum 1 + 2 + 3 + … + 100 odd or even?
q.e: There are 50 odd numbers (an even count → even) and 50 evens. Total 5050, even.

q.t: Every number in the 1–9 magic square is doubled. New magic sum?
q.e: Each line's three numbers are all doubled, so each line sum doubles: 15 × 2 = 30.

q.t: Sequence of heights calls 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. How are they standing?
q.e: Each person has everyone in front taller than them, so heights decrease along the line.
